subject: Latency guardrails & burst mitigation agreement
messages:
From: Marco Silveira <marco@kitepay.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodai.com>
Cc: KitePay Reliability Team <reliability@kitepay.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — latency commitments for hosted API + burst behavior

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the throughput and the console traces. As we get closer to an internal pilot (payment flows), our security and reliability leads want clear commitments on latency for the hosted API and how Redwood handles short, high-concurrency bursts.

Specific asks from KitePay:
- Target quantiles we can include in the contract (we'd like a p50 and p95 baseline).
- Measurement window and aggregation method (rolling 5m? daily buckets?).
- Explicit carveouts for upstream proxy/backplane incidents and customer-driven traffic spikes (we expect some days where campaign traffic triples).
- A short remediation/playbook if we breach targets (credits, canary fallback, dev contact).

I've attached a brief packet with our projected traffic patterns for the pilot (kitedemand-traffic-samples.csv) and a short list of regulatory timing requirements. Can you share a proposed framing we can include in our SOW and a timeline to finalize?

Cheers,
Marco
Marco Silveira
Head of Reliability — KitePay
marco@kitepay.com

Attachments: kitepay_request_packet.pdf, kitedemand-traffic-samples.csv

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodai.com>
To: Marco Silveira <marco@kitepay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask — latency commitments for hosted API + burst behavior

Hi Marco — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed. Thanks for the packet; that traffic sample is helpful.

High-level proposal for contractual language (draft):
- Latency Targets: p50 <= 30 ms, p95 <= 220 ms for the hosted API when measured under normal operational load.
- Measurement Window: rolling 1-hour windows aggregated into daily reporting; p50/p95 reported on a daily rolling basis and measured across successful requests only.
- Burst/Mitigation Carveout: we will exclude transient events where a customer-origin traffic spike (self-inflicted burst > 3x baseline sustained > 15 minutes) or third-party network incidents are the dominant root cause. Transient bursts that resolve within a 30-minute window will be visible in dashboards but may qualify for a transient carveout review if they meet the above criteria.
- Remediation & Credits: If daily p95 exceeds the commitment by >20% for 3 consecutive business days (and is not a qualified carveout), Redwood will: 1) open an incident timeline and provide root-cause analysis within 5 business days, and 2) apply service credits tiered by severity (TBD in SOW).

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling prefix caching for payment-related request paths and a conservative batching policy for synchronous calls to reduce p95 tail.
- For the pilot, we can offer a temporary burst buffer (10% additional dedicated capacity) for the first 60 days at no extra charge to smooth the onboarding curve.

I'll loop in Ben for commercial approval on the addendum language and Lauren to validate measurement phrasing in the master SOW. If this matches KitePay's expectations, I'll circulate a redlineable addendum.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwoodai.com

Attachments: latency-commitment-addendum-draft.docx

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: FYI: KitePay SLO framing and proposed carveout language — need approvals

Team — forwarding KitePay's ask and my proposed framing (below). Quick asks: 
- Ben: can we approve the 60-day free burst buffer for the pilot and the credit banding approach as a commercial concession?
- Lauren: confirm the measurement window language (rolling 1-hour into daily reporting) is defensible for legal/SLA purposes.
- Irene: can you review the carveout criteria wording on network vs. customer-origin traffic and any observability gaps we'll need to instrument?

Quoted below is my outbound to KitePay (same as sent). I attached the draft addendum for review.

Thanks,
Avery

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodai.com>, Marco Silveira <marco@kitepay.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FYI: KitePay SLO framing and proposed carveout language — need approvals

Thanks everyone — reviewed the draft. Ben here: commercial sign-off with two conditions:
1) The temporary 10% burst buffer is approved for the 60-day pilot, but only if KitePay shares the final traffic-sample CSV and authorizes a short-load test during onboarding (we'll schedule a 2-hour ramp test).
2) Credit bands will be defined in the addendum as: minor (p95 exceedance <= 40% for 1 business day) -> 5% service credit; major (p95 exceedance > 40% for >=2 business days) -> 15% credit; severe -> exec review + higher credit. Legal to finalize exact wording.

Lauren/Irene — please flag if the rolling 1-hour -> daily aggregation has known edge cases we should call out before we give KitePay the redline draft.

Marco — if that sounds workable, Avery will send the redlineable addendum and we'll attach the DocuSign link. We expect the final SOW addendum to be agreed before the pilot start.

-Ben
